instruction: Work with FEniCS from the command line and identify three scalar PDE parameters from fixed observation data. For the steps below, run legacy FEniCS with `/home/user/miniconda3/bin/conda run --no-capture-output --prefix /home/user/miniconda3/envs/fenics-legacy python` when working on `parameter_inverse_opt_base.py`. Read /home/user/Desktop/problem_spec.json for the parameter bounds, observation points, observation values, forward-response equation, and the equivalent one-dimensional boundary-value problem used to verify that response with FEniCS. Read /home/user/Desktop/baseline_parameters.json as the initial feasible parameter set. You may use /home/user/Desktop/parameter_inverse_opt_base.py as the starter workflow. Create /home/user/Desktop/parameters.json, /home/user/Desktop/solve_submission.py, and /home/user/Desktop/predictions.json. The parameter file must contain numeric keys E, k, and alpha; keep E in [50000, 250000], k in [1, 20], and alpha in [0.01, 0.25]. predictions.json must report the fixed observation points, unchanged observations, and predictions from the specified response equation. Keep the observation data, forward model, verification PDE, and parameter bounds from the problem specification unchanged.
